title: Know Your Limits: The Law of Grandiosity

chapterBreakdown.gentle: The chapter on grandiosity stays useful because it names a pattern people often feel before they can explain it. This law argues that success, praise, and insulation from contradiction can swell people into grandiosity, causing them to confuse self-image with scale, momentum with invulnerability, and desire with reality. This is why the law focuses on feedback loops. Power, praise, and insulation can build a sealed mental world in which warnings feel petty and boundaries feel beneath the exceptional person. In that state, overreach becomes likely because evidence is being sorted by ego service rather than by truth value. The practical move is practical grandiosity: keep ambition, but pair it with friction, reality tests, hard numbers, dissent, and periodic reductions of scale. The goal is not timidity. It is a self that can still hear correction before circumstances become the teacher. Ambition survives best when scale keeps meeting reality. That softer honesty is already a practical advantage.
